panels.rationale: Single clinical photo of both feet showing interdigital dry cracked/scaling lesions described in caption. Article title is disease-focused on tinea pedis masking psoriasis vulgaris, supporting attribution to tinea pedis with specific captioned manifestation.
panels.attribution_text: Sookdar et al. Psoriasis Vulgaris Masked by Tinea Pedis in Two Unhoused Patients.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.65206. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Draining malodorous lesion between the first and second digits, and dry, cracked areas between the second, third, and fourth digits of both feet.
in_text_mentions: dry and broken areas of skin between the second, third, and fourth digits of both feet. The patient had been experiencing such pruritic lesions on both elbows, as well as portions of the proximal radial and ulnar regions, and the posterior knee areas for several years. During this presentation, the vital signs were within normal limits. On examination, cardiopulmonary and abdominal examinations were normal. The skin examination revealed a draining malodorous lesion between the first and second digits, and dry, cracked areas between the second, third, and fourth digits of both feet (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Single H&E biopsy image from plantar foot in Case 2 diagnosed as tinea pedis. Caption and in-text state hyperkeratosis with thickened stratum corneum and acanthosis; hyphae not readily visualized on H&E but case confirmed as tinea pedis by PAS in Figure 8. Histologic hyperkeratosis maps to moccasin-type plantar hyperkeratosis vocabulary term.
panels.attribution_text: Cohen et al. Tinea Corporis and Tinea Pedis Can Masquerade As Other Cutaneous Conditions in Decedents: Forensic Dermatology of Dermatophyte Infections.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.101452. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 7.
panels.figure_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin-stained slides of tinea pedis in Case 2. Microscopic examination of a biopsy from the plantar foot shows hyperkeratosis, with a thickened stratum corneum consisting of compact orthokeratosis (open black bracket). In contrast to acquired ichthyosis, the granular layer is present beneath the stratum corneum (between the black arrows). The epidermis beneath the stratum corneum is also thickened (acanthosis). Fungal hyphae in the stratum corneum (open black bracket) are not readily visualized on the hematoxylin and eosin-stained sections (hematoxylin and eosin stain, x20).
in_text_mentions: A biopsy of the plantar foot showed thickened stratum corneum (hyperkeratosis) and thickening of the epidermis (acanthosis). Dermatophyte hyphae could not be noticed on the hematoxylin and eosin-stained sections of the epidermis (Figure 7). However, the periodic acid-Schiff-stained sections clearly confirmed the presence of hyphae in the stratum corneum (Figure 8).

plate_findings.evidence: Periodic acid-Schiff-stained low-magnification view (x20) of a plantar foot biopsy showing compact orthokeratosis with black arrows pointing to purple-staining fungal hyphae within the hyperkeratotic stratum corneum.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Genuine patient PAS-stained histopathology from a plantar foot biopsy in a confirmed tinea pedis case (caption explicitly states 'Periodic acid-Schiff-stained slides of tinea pedis in Case 2'), showing fungal hyphae within the hyperkeratotic stratum corneum; directly supports the configured disease. B: Higher-magnification PAS-stained histopathology of the same plantar foot biopsy from a confirmed tinea pedis case, clearly demonstrating septate fungal hyphae in the stratum corneum; directly supports the configured disease.
panels.attribution_text: Cohen et al. Tinea Corporis and Tinea Pedis Can Masquerade As Other Cutaneous Conditions in Decedents: Forensic Dermatology of Dermatophyte Infections.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.101452. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 8.
panels.figure_caption: Periodic acid-Schiff-stained slides of tinea pedis in Case 2. Low (A) and higher (B) magnification views of a biopsy from the plantar foot show compact orthokeratosis overlying the epidermis. Numerous fungal hyphae (black arrows pointing to purple-staining organisms) can be observed within the hyperkeratotic stratum corneum (periodic acid-Schiff stain, x20 (A) and x40 (B)).
in_text_mentions: A biopsy of the plantar foot showed thickened stratum corneum (hyperkeratosis) and thickening of the epidermis (acanthosis).
